content.content:
- name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '6085551023'
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank @org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.Telephone"
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.Email"
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the owner was registered. Defaults to the server's current date when omitted.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allow creating this owner even though another owner already has the same last
            name and address (i.e. they knowingly share a household). Write-only; never persisted.
          type: boolean
          default: false
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: The canonical region derived from the city via the fixed city-to-region table (Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD), or 'UNKNOWN' for any other city.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: Stable code formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>', where LAST3 is the upper-cased first three letters of the last name and NNNN is a global 4-digit zero-padded sequence assigned at registration.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household id
              description: Stable identifier shared by owners that knowingly share a household (same last name and address). Assigned only when an owner joins an existing household via 'sharesHousehold'.
              type: string
              example: 'HH-0A1B2C3D4E5F'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: The number of existing owners that shared this owner's first and last name (case-insensitively) at the time this owner was created.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: Stable code formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>', where YY is the last two digits of the registrationDate year.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007-M26'
              readOnly: true
            membershipTier:
              title: Membership tier
              description: "'SILVER' when the owner has no namesakes (namesakeCount is 0) and an email is present, otherwise 'BRONZE'."
              type: string

The change is complete and the full suite passes. Here's a summary of what I implemented.

## Change: registration date must fall on a business day

The **effective** registration date — whether supplied in the request or defaulted to the server date — now rolls forward to the next Monday when it lands on a Saturday or Sunday. Everything derived from it uses the adjusted date.

### Where the logic lives

- **`util/BusinessDay.java`** (new) — a small, single-responsibility pure function `rollForward(LocalDate)`: Saturday → +2 days, Sunday → +1 day, weekdays unchanged. This is the one reusable unit; every other site delegates to it.

- **`model/Owner.java`** — the `@PrePersist` hook now defaults a missing date to `LocalDate.now()` **and** rolls the effective date forward via `BusinessDay.rollForward`. This guarantees the persistence-layer invariant (the stored `registrationDate` is always a business day) for any JPA persist path, which is what the acceptance test asserts. Because the membership number is derived in `OwnerMapper` from the stored `registrationDate`, its year segment automatically uses the adjusted date.

- **`service/ClinicService[Impl].java`** — added `resolveRegistrationDate(LocalDate)` (default-to-now + roll forward) as the request-time resolver, and changed `isDailyOwnerLimitReached()` to `isDailyOwnerLimitReached(LocalDate registrationDate)` so the daily create-limit counts owners per **adjusted business day** rather than the raw server date.

- **`rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — `addOwner` now resolves the effective business-day date, sets it on the owner (so both the persisted value and the derived membership number use it), and checks the daily limit against that adjusted date.

### Behaviour change captured
A supplied weekend date is now rolled forward too (previously left untouched), the membership-number year segment follows the adjusted date, and the daily limit buckets owners by adjusted business day.

`./mvnw -o test` → **BUILD SUCCESS**, `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` (the acceptance test is the only test class in the suite).
